subject: Re: Post-call: Soprano Health evaluation runbook, dataset & scoring
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
To: Asha Patel <asha.patel@sopranohealth.com>, EngOps <engops@sopranohealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>

Subject: Post-call recap & next steps — Redwood-run eval (dataset, scoring, timing)

Thanks again for the time today — good conversation. Short recap and concrete next steps so we can run a customer-specific eval on Redwood and show comparative performance quickly.

Call summary (brief):
- Goal: validate model fit for Soprano’s triage assistant (clinical routing + FAQ fallback) on a 1k-sample subset and a held-out 10k benchmark.
- Primary success criteria: intent-class accuracy, slot-level F1 (entities), and hallucination rate under 3% (operational definition below).
- Preference: deterministic outputs for benchmark runs (we’ll use temperature=0.0 / greedy decoding).

Proposed Redwood-run plan (what we will do):
1) You share a de-identified 1k sample (JSONL) + a schema file (see attachment soprano_eval-template.csv). We’ll run the sample in our hosted sandbox for initial diagnostics.
2) We'll run two candidate models and a quantized variant: redwood-instruct-6.1 (baseline), redwood-chat-7b, and redwood-chat-7b-q4_8bit to check latency/cost tradeoffs.
3) We’ll run deterministic prompts, produce structured JSON outputs, and score against your gold labels.
4) Deliverables: runbook with CLI commands, a results spreadsheet (per-case metrics), confusion matrices, and a short video walkthrough.

Dataset & format (required):
- JSONL, one object per line. Required fields: id (string), prompt (string), gold (string OR object), metadata (object — optional). Example line attached in soprano_sample-1000.jsonl.
- If samples contain PHI, please replace names/IDs with consistent tokens (e.g., [PATIENT_001]). We can accept an encrypted bundle or run within a Private instance if needed.

Scoring & pass criteria (high level):
- Intent accuracy (exact match) >= 92%: primary gate for model fit.
- Entity F1 (micro-average) >= 88%: slot extraction for routing.
- Hallucination detection: we run a combination of rule-based checks and embedding-similarity checks; target false positive rate <= 3%.
- Semantic similarity fallback: embeddings.cosine_similarity(gold, response) >= 0.82 considered acceptable for free-text QA items.

Next steps / timeline:
- Asha: confirm you’ll share 1k sample + schema by EOD Wed 7/7.
- Marissa/Redwood: run initial evaluation and return results by EOD Fri 7/9.
- Optional follow-up: deep 10k benchmark and SLA discussion pending results.

Attachments: soprano_sample-1000.jsonl (sample), soprano_eval-template.csv (schema), prompt-templates-v1.txt (recommended prompt scaffolds).

If it’s helpful I can also provide a short dockerized harness to run locally — we have a CLI that does everything below.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.inference

Asha — quick answers + the CLI runbook & scoring spec below. I’ll also drop the Drive prompt-set to the link in the thread.

Embeddings & similarity: we use redwood-embed-2-small for cosine similarity by default; cosine >= 0.82 on that embedding is our operational threshold for acceptable semantic match, but we always surface the raw score so you can tune it.

Hallucination detection (summary of rule set):
- Rule-based triggers: presence of hallucination keywords (e.g., fabricated claim indicators), numeric inconsistency checks, and unsupported confident assertions for out-of-scope topics.
- Semantic-check: low embedding similarity between the answer and any supported evidence snippets (if you provide documents).
- PHI handling: we never infer PHI replacements during scoring; if gold contains a PHI token we only compare non-PII fields. If you need, we can run the eval in your VPC for full PHI compliance.

Redwood eval CLI example (sandbox run; deterministic):
- redwood eval run --input soprano_sample-1000.jsonl --model redwood-instruct-6.1 --prompt-templates prompt-templates-v1.txt --temperature 0.0 --max-tokens 256 --output soprano_results_redwood-instruct-6.1.jsonl --batch-size 8
- repeat with --model redwood-chat-7b and --model redwood-chat-7b-q4_8bit to capture latency/cost.

Scoring config (we will use this YAML-style sheet in the harness):
- intent: exact_match
- entities: token_span_f1
- free_text: [rouge_l, embedding_cosine (model=redwood-embed-2-small, pass>=0.82)]
- hallucination: combined_rule_score >= 0.7 triggers manual review

Pass/fail: we’ll mark a model as candidate-ready if intent >= 92% AND entities F1 >= 88% AND hallucination_rate <= 3%. If those fail we’ll recommend ensemble/chain-of-thought prompt patterns and re-run.

Deliverables we’ll upload to the Drive link: per-case CSV, summary sheet with thresholds, and a condensed regression deck.

Internal note: if you want the run inside a Private instance for PHI, we’ll need a security questionnaire completed and a quick infra sync.

I’ll start the sandbox runs as soon as you share the 1k.

—Marissa

Internal check — copying the plan into this thread so we don’t lose it. A few operational items to add before we run: 

1) Canary samples: add 50 canary prompts (immutable) to detect regressions vs baseline every week.
2) Regression alerting: add a CI job that re-runs the 1k sample on nightlies and alerts if intent drops >2% or entities F1 drops >3%. Integrate with PagerDuty and create a low-noise Slack channel for triage.
3) Scoring stability: use deterministic seeding and disable sampling; store raw logits in case we need to audit.

Karthik — can you prepare the canary set and add the CI job to the repo? Marissa — let me know if we should surface cost estimates for the different quantization options in the initial delivery.

Thanks,
Ben
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
